shouldFix.title: /v1Lineage.standing states that this artifact's predecessor is v2, while /basedOn/predecessor is v3 - the CLAUDE-V3-S1 repair reintroduces the exact discrepancy it was created to remove
detail: My v3 finding S-1 was titled 'The top-level predecessor block still names v1 as this artifact's predecessor, unlabeled, while basedOn names v2'. Its substance was a disagreement between a lineage block and /basedOn about what this artifact's predecessor is.

v4's repair moves the five unlabeled top-level keys (/predecessor, /predecessorSha256, /predecessorVerdict, /predecessorVerdictSha256, /predecessorVerdictFindings) into a labelled /v1Lineage block. I confirmed all five are gone from the top level and their values are carried unchanged inside /v1Lineage, so the relocation and labelling half is done correctly.

But /v1Lineage/standing reads, in full: 'INHERITED v1-generation lineage record; this artifact's predecessor is v2 at basedOn.' In v4, /basedOn/predecessor is 'docs/coop/artifacts/permission-truth-tables.v3.json'. So the sentence asserts v2 where the artifact's own basedOn says v3.

This is not carried text that merely went stale: /v1Lineage does not exist in v3, so the sentence is newly authored in v4. It appears to have been written from v3's frame of reference, where 'predecessor is v2 at basedOn' would have been correct, and not rebased onto v4.

The artifact demonstrates elsewhere that the correct formulation was known. /honestyRepairsFromV3[0] states it precisely: 'the unlabeled top-level predecessor* block is renamed to /v1Lineage and qualified as inherited v1-generation lineage; this artifact's predecessor is v2 at basedOn (v3) / v3 at basedOn (v4).' The repair log carries the generation-aware version; the field it describes does not.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: The whole purpose of CLAUDE-V3-S1 was that a lineage block must not contradict /basedOn about the artifact's predecessor. The repair fixes the v1-versus-v2 contradiction and installs a v2-versus-v3 one in the same field. A reader who consults /v1Lineage to answer 'what is v4's predecessor?' - which is exactly what the labelled block invites - gets the wrong answer, and gets it from the field added to make that question answerable.
shouldFix.whyNotABlocker: Nothing in the truth tables, refusal families, linearization or any binding surface depends on this sentence, and /basedOn carries the correct answer two keys away. The defect is confined to one clause of one descriptive field.
shouldFix.remedy: One token: 'this artifact's predecessor is v3 at basedOn.' Better still, make it generation-proof - 'this artifact's predecessor is the artifact recorded at /basedOn' - so the next successor cannot strand it again, which is the failure mode this field has now exhibited twice.

advisories.title: /environmentStanding/note changed, while the closed roster names that parent only as 'COORD pin (live re-measure only)'
advisories.detail: basedOn.method states the rule strictly: 'Every path neither the roster nor succession metadata names is unchanged from v3.' My recursive diff found 24 changed paths and 23 map cleanly onto roster entries. The twenty-fourth is /environmentStanding/note, which gains the sentence 'v4 re-measured live COORD after D-103; the previous live pin is at reMeasurementAtV3.' The roster entry covering that parent reads '/environmentStanding COORD pin (live re-measure only)', and the parenthetical narrows it to the pin. I record this as advisory rather than a finding because the parent path is named, the added sentence is the annotation of the very re-measure the roster authorizes, and the change is separately disclosed at /honestyRepairsFromV3[2] and /reMeasurementAtV4 - nothing is concealed. It is worth tightening because this roster names sub-paths precisely everywhere else ('/registerRowCarriedWhole/parsedCellsDerivedFrom', '/reviewGuidance/forTheIndependentReviewer (append)'), so the narrow phrasing reads as deliberate.
advisories.notBlocking: No substantive content is hidden; the added sentence is true and I verified the measurement it describes.
